title: Deterministic and programmable generation of mechanical multipartite entangled states
authors: Isabelle Franzen, Max-Emanuel Kern, Q. Rumman Rahman, Igor Kladarić, Stefano Marti, Yiwen Chu, Zhi-Yuan Wei, Matteo Fadel
abstract: Multimode mechanical resonators offer a large set of densely packed, long-lived bosonic modes within a single compact device, making them attractive for quantum simulation, quantum information processing, and quantum-enhanced sensing. Many such applications rely on multipartite entanglement, yet deterministic mechanical entanglement has so far been largely limited to pairs of modes. Here we demonstrate the deterministic and programmable preparation of multipartite entangled states among the phonon modes of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator coupled to a superconducting transmon qubit. By sequentially applying optimal-control-engineered isometries between the qubit and successive modes, we generate matrix product states of bond dimension two, including $W$, Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ), and cluster states. We fully characterize these states via quantum state tomography and certify genuine multipartite entanglement among up to four modes. We further demonstrate correlated-noise sensing by exploiting the complementary decoherence responses of the stored $W$ and GHZ states, isolating inter-mode phase correlations from local decoherence and placing quantitative bounds on collective dephasing. Our results establish a scalable approach to preparing multipartite entangled states in mechanical systems, with promising applications in multiparameter sensing and tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects.
summary: This work demonstrates a scalable method to deterministically create complex multipartite entangled states (like W and GHZ states) in mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting qubits. By combining optimal control techniques with quantum state tomography, the authors not only prepare these states but also develop a robust sensing protocol that isolates collective noise effects from local decoherence.
main_problem: The paper addresses the deterministic and programmable generation of multipartite entangled states among mechanical modes, which is crucial for quantum simulation and sensing.
main_result: They successfully demonstrated the preparation of W, GHZ, and cluster states in a mechanical system and developed a method to quantify inter-mode phase correlations by isolating them from local decoherence.
method: The protocol uses optimal-control-engineered isometries implemented via a superconducting transmon qubit coupled to a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator (HBAR). State characterization involves quantum state tomography and entanglement witnesses.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a circuit quantum acoustics (cQAD) setup involving a transmon qubit coupled to multiple phonon modes in an HBAR. The dynamics are analyzed using Hamiltonian descriptions and master equations to model decoherence.
key_observables: Fidelity ($F$), Genuine Multipartite Entanglement (GME) witnesses ($	ext{Tr}[\hat{W}ho]$), and the ratio $R_N(t)$ used to estimate collective dephasing rates.
important_parameters: Bond dimension two (for MPS), coupling strengths ($g_k$), and decoherence rates ($\gamma^{(k)}_1, \gamma^{(k)}_\phi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often focuses on the two lowest Fock states ($\{|0angle_k, |1angle_k\}$) of each mode, and the decoherence analysis relies on specific master equation forms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the HBAR device, the algorithm for MPS preparation using isometries, and show experimental/simulated fidelities for W, GHZ, and cluster states for various particle numbers.
paper_structure: The paper moves from demonstrating the physical protocol for state preparation (using isometries and tomography) to analyzing the theoretical robustness of these states against decoherence (comparing W vs. GHZ decay rates).
why_interesting: The combination of a solid-state mechanical system (HBAR) with superconducting qubits to generate and test complex entangled states is highly relevant for scalable quantum hardware development and quantum sensing.

FIG. 2. Fidelities of the prepared W, GHZ and cluster states, and density matrices. a) Experimental and simulated fidelities for W states prepared on different numbers of modes. b,c) Real part of representative density matrices for W2 and W3 states reconstructed from full state tomography. d,e,f) and g,h,i) show the same for GHZ and cluster states, respectively. Simulations include decoherence during the state-preparation sequence but not the sequential tomographic readout. For W states the decrease of the measured fidelities thus originates mainly from the readout, while for GHZ and cluster states the decrease reflects decoherence during the optimal-control pulses (see main text).

FIG. 3. Free evolution of W and GHZ coherences. a) Coherence C(t), normalized to its value at t = 0, of W states with N = 2, 3 modes as a function of the free evolution time t. Lines show fits to Ae−t/τ + B, with the extracted decay times τ given in the legend. b) Pairwise coherences ckl(t) of the W3 state, fitted in the same way. c) Same as panel a, but for GHZ states. Unlike for W states, the GHZ decay rate depends on N. This dependence is here quantitatively explained by local decoherence alone, without any contribution from correlated dephasing (see main text for details).
